visual.text: You know your phone. They know everything else.
Skill Swap Saturdays — where teenagers and seniors teach each other.
A teenage boy and an elderly woman laugh over a phone. A half-finished rattan basket sits on the table between them.

Your grandmother can fold a ketupat in ten seconds. Can you? Spend one Saturday morning a month with a senior from your neighbourhood. You show them how to make a video call, pay a bill online and spot a scam message. They show you something no app can teach.

visual.title: What one morning looks like
items: 9.30 am — You teach: one phone skill, one-to-one
10.30 am — They teach: cooking, weaving, repairs or dialect
11.30 am — Everyone shares what they learnt

visual.text: “I came to teach Mdm Goh how to pay with her phone. I left knowing how to sew on a button, and with an invitation to lunch every week.” — Irfan, 15
No experience needed. Ages 13 to 18. Counts towards your Values in Action hours.
Sign up by 30 June — places are limited to 40 pairs
Tampines West Community Library · every second Saturday of the month

questions.text: Look at the headline: ‘You know your phone. They know everything else.’ What does it suggest teenagers can gain from the programme?

scheme.answer: Seniors have a great deal of knowledge and skills outside technology, and teenagers can learn these from them.
accept: Teenagers can pick up many useful skills or life lessons from older people that they do not have themselves.

seeds.text: It suggests that seniors know a lot of things other than technology, and teenagers can learn all these from them.
Teens are only good with phones, but the old folks have plenty of other skills to pass on to them.
It suggests that teenagers can become better at using their phones.
They can gain a lot from joining the programme.
Seniors do not know how to use phones.

questions.text: ‘They show you something no app can teach.’ What is the writer suggesting about the skills that seniors have?

scheme.answer: Their skills are hands-on and personal, so they cannot be learnt from a phone or the internet — they are special and worth learning in person.
accept: The skills are valuable because technology cannot replace them.

seeds.text: The writer suggests their skills are special because you cannot get them from technology, only from the person.
